title: EARLY 1900'S JAPANESE TANSY CH...
reason: Genuine looking early 1900s Japanese four-drawer tansu with original iron fittings and old writing, misspelt in the title so likely to be missed by searchers; solid mid-range piece.
findings: Six photos (front, lock plate close-up, two close-ups of a paper label, back/side with paper strip, drawers open). Narrow four-drawer Japanese chest (tansu); the title's 'tansy' is a misspelling that will make it harder to find in searches. Plain timber, probably sugi (Japanese cedar) with a dark worn finish. Each drawer has an iron lock plate with keyhole and boss and a forged iron swing handle; an iron carrying ring is on the side; drawer interiors are pale unfinished softwood. Remnants of old paper labels with ink characters survive on some drawer fronts (heavily abraded; one character looks like 甲 or 田, the rest unreadable). A pasted paper strip down the back carries two columns of cursive Japanese brush writing (kuzushiji), not legible at this resolution; old paper like this is commonly seen on genuine old merchant chests and supports age. No maker's name, seal or date found. Construction and fittings look Meiji to Taisho in style, which fits the 'early 1900's' title.
condition: Heavy honest wear: scraped and flaking surface, scuffs and dark staining, chipped and worn edges on the drawer rails and top, paper label remnants. Iron fittings are rusty but complete; drawers slide out and look complete; keys not seen; no obvious structural cracks in the photos.
rescore_note: Looks like a genuine Meiji to Taisho sugi tansu with original iron fittings, complete drawers and old paper writing; plain, smallish and heavily worn with no maker or seal, so a mid-range piece in the $80-200 band. Estimate only, no live comps.
